The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20
and N-29-20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meeting to order at 6:31 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith, and Commissioners Jeffrey
  Jennings, John Mazza, and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Assistant City Attorney; Richard Mollica, Planning
  Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning Director; Troy Spayd, Assistant Public
  Works Director; Patricia Salazar, Senior Administrative Analyst; and Rebecca Evans,
  Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda as recommended by staff, hearing Item 1 B prior to Item 1 A.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on December 27, 2021.

  Vice Chair Smith stated that Commissioner~zza should resign or be removed based on
  his recent comments regarding City Hall staff and consultants in the Jefferson Wagner
  affidavit. He recommended that the Department Heads should move to have Commissioner
  Mazza removed if he is not willing to resign.

Assistant Planning Director Fernandez presented the staff report.

Disclosures: Commissioners Jennings, Mazza, Wetton, and Chair Hill

Chair Hill noted that the Commission had received letters regarding the fact that
Commissioner Jennings worked on his home with Doug Burdge after the Woolsey
Fire. Mr. Tobias alleged that a special deal was made and asked Chair Hill asked
Commissioner Jennings for a response to provide more clarity.

Commissioner Jennings consulted with Assistant City Attorney Rusin to see if there
was any reason for him to be recused. The Commissioner had no special deal for
services from Doug Burdge who has acted as his architect for his Woolsey Fire
rebuild. The Commissioner had no reduction in fees based on his position with the
Planning Commission. Nothing in Commissioner Jennings’ relationship with Doug
Burdge would impact his ability to be impartial in the hearing. The Hakirn brothers
are the owners of the project. The project architect would receive financial benefit
regardless of plan approval.

Assistant City Attorney Rusin provided clarification on conflict issues requiring
recusal: 1) Political Reform Act—compensation such as income from something
else. In this case Commissioner Jennings paid the money and did not receive it. If
he was getting a special rate not available to others in a similar situation, he would
need to disclose this on Form 700 and if the value exceeded the limit, recuse
himself. Doug Burdge confirmed that this is not the case. 2) Unacceptable
probability of actual bias toward a decision based on prior public comments
indicating a Commissioner premade a decision or has such a close relationship with
an applicant, they would not be able to make an impartial decision. There is no
prohibition against a Councilmember or Commissioner hiring a local architect,
attorney, doctor, or anybody else in the City and that alone does not create a bias.
In this situation, there was no requirement by the Fair Political Practices
Commission that Commissioner Jennings recuse himself.

Doug Burdge clarified his firm voted to provide a twenty percent discount on their
services to any clients who lost their homes or suffered damage in the Woolsey
fires across the board. This included about thirty rebuilds and his firm has contracts
that provide evidence of these terms. The decision was based on the firm’s
relationship to the community and the breadth of Woolsey Fire damage.

  section of the public hearing.

  Speakers: Steven Hakim, Alexander Hakim and Doug Burdge, applicant team; Judy
  Ettinger, Jo Drummond, Suzannah Owens, Nick Eliopoulos, Brianna Ickes, Lisa
  Sockolov, Laurie Albert, Stephen Albert, Stella Allan, Patt Healy, Jefferson
  Wagner, Ryan Embree, Scott Dittrich and Bill Sampson.

  The applicant team provided rebuttal to public comment.

  As there were no other speakers present, Chair Hill closed the public comment
  portion of the public hearing and returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Commission discussed the project and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  continue Items 1 A and 1 B to April 4, 2022, directing staff to contact the Regional
  Water Quality Control Board for clarification on whether the project qualifies as
  exempt under Table 4-zz.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

  This item was continued to the April 4, 2022 Regular Planning Commission
  meeting.
